---
title: "Calling compute functions"
---

Every published Chart Data result is a keyword-only `compute_*` function. There
is no evaluation context to open, and no `set_*` step that writes cells before
a solve. You pass the leaves that function needs and it returns that one result.

# Arguments are keyword-only

A function that depends on a single scalar looks like ordinary Python:

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import compute_tailored_stress_market_financing_applicable

compute_tailored_stress_market_financing_applicable(
    country="Ghana",
    input6_tailored_tests_enabled="On",
)
```

Switching tailored tests off is another explicit call, not a mutation of a
shared workbook object:

```{python}
compute_tailored_stress_market_financing_applicable(
    country="Ghana",
    input6_tailored_tests_enabled="Off",
)
```

Positional arguments are rejected. That is deliberate: a 60-argument DSA call
is unsafe to line up by position.

# Scalars stay scalars; series are named tensors

A country name, a discount rate, or an on/off flag is a bare Python value. A
time series or an instrument schedule is a typed tensor from
`lic_dsf_2025_08_12.data`. The tensor carries the axis names and legal keys so
a value is never silently aligned to the wrong year or instrument.

A plain list is not accepted:

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import data
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.tensor import SchemaError

try:
    compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable(
        input6_commodity_group_relevant=["Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"],
        input6_tailored_tests_enabled=data.INPUT6_TAILORED_TESTS_ENABLED_DEFAULT,
        input3_input_3_macro_exports_of_goods_and_services=data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_EXPORTS_OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES_DEFAULT,
        input3_input_3_macro_exports_commodity_fuel=data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_EXPORTS_COMMODITY_FUEL_DEFAULT,
        input3_input_3_macro_exports_commodity_non_fuel=data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_EXPORTS_COMMODITY_NON_FUEL_DEFAULT,
        input3_input_3_macro_imports_commodity_fuel_enter_as_a_positive_number=data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_IMPORTS_COMMODITY_FUEL_ENTER_AS_A_POSITIVE_NUMBER_DEFAULT,
        input3_input_3_macro_imports_commodity_non_fuel_enter_as_a_positive_number=data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_IMPORTS_COMMODITY_NON_FUEL_ENTER_AS_A_POSITIVE_NUMBER_DEFAULT,
    )
except SchemaError as error:
    print(error)
```

Build or copy a typed series instead. The next page shows how to revise one
coordinate of a template series.

# Load the template snapshot

The generated `data` module stores the IDA21 template values as
`<ARGUMENT>_DEFAULT`. Rating and chart functions take several dozen arguments;
gathering those snapshot values by name is the practical way to start a run:

```{python}
import inspect

from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import data


def template_inputs(compute):
    """Return the 2025-08-12 template snapshot for every argument of `compute`."""
    return {
        name: getattr(data, f"{name.upper()}_DEFAULT")
        for name in inspect.signature(compute).parameters
    }


inputs = template_inputs(compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable)
compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable(**inputs)
```

Override only the assumptions you are changing. The rest stay at the template
vintage:

```{python}
inputs["input6_tailored_tests_enabled"] = "Off"
compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable(**inputs)
```

# What comes back

Scalar Chart Data cells return a `float` or a `str` -- a 0/1 flag, a rating
word such as `"High"`, or a most-extreme-shock label such as `"Exports"`.

Chart rows return a tensor keyed by the same coordinates the workbook uses
(`SCENARIO`, `TIME_PERIOD`, and similar). Convert that tensor to records with
`as_records` so a table or a plot never depends on positional indexes. The
[chart series](chart-series.qmd) page works through that shape.
